_about: The standard program protocol every Arm B scenario assumes. Shown on the About page and available from every scenario. A scenario may state an exception in its visit text.
name: Standard community paramedicine program protocol
summary: A medical director's standing orders for a community paramedic working alone from a response vehicle, with a provider reachable by phone at all times.

sections.title: Provider access
items: A supervising provider is reachable by phone 24 hours a day for consultation and orders.
A same-day clinic or urgent-care slot can be arranged for any patient seen before mid-afternoon; after that, same-day evaluation means the emergency department.
A return home visit within 24–48 hours can be scheduled at the paramedic's discretion.

sections.title: Point-of-care testing carried
items: i-STAT with CHEM8+ (sodium, potassium, chloride, total CO2, BUN, creatinine, glucose, ionized calcium, hematocrit), CG4+ (blood gas and lactate) and PT/INR cartridges.
Glucometer, HemoCue hemoglobin, urine dipstick, urine ketone strips, rapid influenza and group A strep antigen tests.
12-lead ECG with transmission to the supervising provider.
Venous samples can be drawn for send-out; results return in 24–72 hours.

sections.title: The paramedic may, without a call
items: Assess, obtain vitals and point-of-care labs, and document.
Give oral fluids or oral rehydration solution and assist with a meal.
Treat hypoglycemia per EMS protocol.
Assist the patient with medications already prescribed to them, and reconcile the medication list against the record.
Arrange home health, dietitian, social work, durable equipment or scheduled transport referrals.
Provide education and teach-back.

sections.title: The paramedic may, on a provider's phone order
items: Hold, adjust or restart a prescribed medication (for example a diuretic dose or a warfarin dose per the anticoagulation protocol).
Give the first dose of an oral antibiotic from the vehicle kit while a prescription is sent to the pharmacy.
Draw and send additional labs and schedule the recheck.

sections.title: The paramedic may not
items: Start, stop or change a prescription on their own authority.
Give intravenous fluids or intravenous medications except under EMS protocol while awaiting transport.
Leave a patient at home whose findings meet the program's emergent criteria.

sections.title: Disposition tiers
items: Tier 1 — Emergent ED transport now.
Tier 2 — Same-day evaluation, non-emergent (clinic, urgent care or ED, by scheduled or private transport).
Tier 3 — PCP or clinic within 24–48 hours.
Tier 4 — Manage in place with follow-up or care coordination (including a provider phone consult and a return visit).
